assertions.name: n_integer_ranks_satisfying_full_bar_condition
assertions.source: sympy exact; ALL of them -- it is an identity of the family

description: M3 contains sigma_n, which the bar involution inverts, so the bar-partner of the Markov parameter z is z - h, not z. Under the correct condition bar(z) = z - h, convention D holds and C fails -- reversing the coefficient-half verdict of #4767/#4802.

interpretation.the_dilemma_dissolves: #4802 concluded bar-invariance and a fibre reading are incompatible at every rank. That holds for the coefficient-half condition bar(z) = z, and that negative is reproduced here. But M3 contains sigma_n, which bar inverts, so the condition the axiom actually supports is bar(z) = z - h -- and THAT condition is an identity of the whole fibre family, verified for symbolic N (equivalently z_N = h/(1 - q^(-2N))). Bar-covariance and the fibre reading are not competing desiderata; they are the SAME condition. There was never a trade-off to make.
interpretation.why_C_fails: Convention C is not a member of the family at any fixed rank: solving z_C = h/(1-q^(-2N)) for N returns a q-dependent expression, so C's implied rank varies with q. The N = 2.5995 of #4766/#4802 is a pointwise inversion at q_0, not a rank. That is why C satisfies the coefficient-half condition and fails the full one.
interpretation.same_error_class_as_item_2: Like eigenbasis-structural-lemmas item 2 (PR #4826), a bar claim about an object living inside the algebra was computed with the coefficient half alone, dropping the sigma -> sigma^{-1} half.
interpretation.what_this_does_not_settle: Scope (a): it removes the stated grounds for preferring C. The >= 8 corpus sites hard-coding C and the owner reservation recorded in #4767 are untouched and not weighed here.

caveats: Rests on tau(x sigma_n^{-1}) = (z - h) tau(x), which follows from M3 plus sigma^{-1} = sigma - h (verified) and LINEARITY of tau. It further assumes the Markov trace is bar-compatible, tau(bar y) = bar(tau y); that compatibility is the standard Ocneanu-trace property but is asserted here, not proved.
Scope (a). Removes the bar-invariance argument for convention C; does not by itself decide the convention, and does not touch the >= 8 corpus sites that hard-code C.
